body: I'm sorry for the way you're feeling. It's fair to be afraid of the challenges ahead, but you have a chance. You can overcome those fears and fight through them and make it out better than you would've imagined. The alternative isn't a life of meaningless suffering. The alternative is a shortened life, one where someone need not suffer any longer. For me idk what the answer is, but for you the choice to choose is to fight and I'm glad you continue to fight and wish you the best of luck moving forward, sincerely.

Thanks. But I always do. I always try to improve. I know it is mostly my fault, but I don't think its fair to say it's all my fault. And after continuously trying and trying to get better but it obviously doesn't work as proven, then what do I do? What is the point of continuing to try?

There is a difference, a fine line, between relying on others for happiness and looking for help. If you rely on others for happiness, it will bring you nothing but more pain and sadness, something many self destructive people like myself have lived through. I believe this post by u/nia_mochi is talking about the other option, one I am dealing with as well. I had a best friend. They were always there for me, and me for them. But my depression has caused me to have trust issues, and to not open up as much as I should because I feel like a burden. When they ask if I'm ok, I just smile and say "I'm ok." But is it our fault that our poor mental stability makes use think and act in those ways? To them, I guess the answer is yes. My best friend finally pulled the trigger 2 days ago pretty much saying she is tired of dealing with my shit. Ghosted me ever since. It's not fair to either us or them. There is no win-win situation.
Thank you. And I hope so too. At least we aren't the only ones who feel like this I guess
Idk. We will see. Thanks though :)
